bib.title: Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning: A Recurrent Depth Approach

read.skipped: Body, tables, Appendix A (implementation, Table 6) read in full. Reference list (from ~offset 63684) skimmed; Appendix B latent-space figure pages (axis numbers only) and Appendix C dataset tables 7-8 skimmed (dataset names/licences, not individually recorded).

question: Can a language model with a weight-shared recurrent block, trained at multi-billion-parameter scale with random iteration counts, improve its reasoning by running more iterations in latent space at test time?
hypothesis: Training with a randomly sampled number of recurrent iterations lets the model use extra test-time recurrence to improve on reasoning tasks, without chain-of-thought data or longer context.
contributions: A depth-recurrent transformer (prelude, recurrent core, coda) with input injection and random initial state, trained with randomly sampled iteration counts and truncated backpropagation
A single large-scale run: 3.5B parameters, about 800B tokens on 4096 AMD MI250X GPUs on Frontier
Benchmark evidence that performance rises with test-time recurrence, up to a compute load equivalent to 50B parameters
Zero-shot per-token adaptive compute, KV-cache sharing, continuous CoT and self-speculative decoding
Latent-space trajectory analysis (convergence, orbits, sliders, path independence)
Release of model, code, data and intermediate checkpoints

method.summary: A decoder-only transformer split into prelude (2 layers), a 4-layer recurrent core iterated r times with the embedded input re-injected each step from a random initial state, and a 2-layer coda. Trained once at 3.5B parameters for about 795-800B tokens with r drawn per micro-batch from a log-normal Poisson distribution (mean 32 plus 1) and gradients through only the last 8 iterations. Evaluated at r from 1 to 64 on lm-eval-harness, math and code benchmarks.
method.task: language-model pretraining with recurrent depth; test-time compute scaling

datasets.name: Pretraining mixture (public sources, Appendix C Tables 7-8)
datasets.size: about 800B tokens seen (795B stated); mixture shares: generic-text 28.71%, code 25.36%, scientific-text 18.73%, synthetic-text 8.14%, longform-text 7.50%, math 6.14%, generic-instruct 2.09%, Q&A-text 1.58%, math-instruct 1.51%, writing-instruct 0.12%, misc-reasoning 0.11%
datasets.source: all publicly available; instruction data mixed directly into pretraining
datasets.preprocessing: BPE tokenizer (65536 vocab) trained on the instruction-data split; documents packed to sequences of 4096; document ends lacking previous context discarded except some long math sources; <|begin_text|> token at document start

datasets.name: Fixed validation set
datasets.split: held out; perplexity at r in [1,4,8,16,32,64]

datasets.name: lm-eval-harness tasks (ARC-E/C, HellaSwag, MMLU, OBQA, PiQA, SciQ, WinoGrande), GSM8K, GSM8K CoT, Minerva MATH, MathQA, MBPP, HumanEval, MT-Bench
datasets.source: standard public benchmarks; code via bigcode-bench

models.name: Huginn-0125
models.params: 3.5B (about 1.5B prelude and head, 1.5B recurrent core, 0.5B tied embedding)
models.architecture: decoder-only transformer, shape (l_P,l_R,l_C)=(2,4,2), sandwich RMSNorm, RoPE base 50000, gated SiLU MLP, adapter on concat(s_i,e)
models.init_from: scratch (Takase et al. 2024 init, variance 2/(5h), out-projections 1/(5hl))
models.layers: 2 prelude + 4 recurrent + 2 coda = 8 real; effective depth 2+4r+2 = 132 at r=32

other.biases: learnable on queries and keys only

models.name: Fixed-depth baseline (same architecture, one pass through core)
Amber, Pythia (2.8b/6.9b/12b), OLMo-1B, OLMo-7B, OLMo-7B-0424, OLMo-7B-0724, OLMo-2-1124-7B, starcoder2-3b/7b

training.objective: next-token cross-entropy, expectation over data and random recurrence count r ~ log-normal Poisson: tau ~ N(log(rbar)-sigma^2/2, sigma), r ~ Poisson(e^tau)+1, with sigma=1/2
training.optimizer: Adam with decoupled weight decay (beta1=0.9, beta2=0.95), update clipping, epsilon removed; gradient clipping at 1
training.lr: 5e-4 stated in optimizer paragraph; final main run used peak 4e-5 (failed run 1 used 4e-4)
training.lr_schedule: warm-up then constant; never cooled down
training.batch_size: 16M tokens per step (1 sequence per GPU x 4096 GPUs)
training.regularisation: truncated backpropagation through last k=8 iterations; locked-step sampling of one r per micro-batch synchronised across workers
training.hardware: Frontier (ORNL), AMD MI250X, 4096 GPUs (512 nodes), data parallel with ZeRO-1 optimizer sharding and per-iteration gradient checkpointing
training.compute: 52-64 TFLOP/s per GPU (41-51% AFU), 1-1.2M tokens/s; single node 108.75 TFLOP/s (87% AFU, 57% MFU); about 212-262 exaFLOP/s per segment
training.wall_clock: 21 segments of up to 12 hours, mostly early December 2024

other.lr_discrepancy: Section 4.1 prints eta = 5e-4, Section 4.3 says the successful run dropped peak LR to 4e-5; the text does not reconcile these
other.small_scale_checks: trained reliably up to 10B tokens before the main run
other.ema: EMA over last 75 checkpoints, beta 0.9, dilation 7, applied post hoc

inference.decoding: recurrence r set at test time (1-64); benchmark protocol follows lm-eval-harness; decoding settings for generation not stated
inference.samples: single evaluation per setting; arithmetic study averages 50 trials per measurement
inference.prompting: zero-shot for most lm-eval tasks; GSM8K CoT 8-way few-shot as multiturn with chat template; HellaSwag and HumanEval zero-shot no chat template; Table 2 reports with and without a system prompt

parameters.adaptive_exit: stop iterating when KL between successive steps < 5e-4
parameters.kv_cache_budget: entry i mod k, tested k in {4, 8, 16}
parameters.continuous_cot: warm-start s0 with last state of previous token

eval.protocol: lm-eval harness and bigcode-bench; no seeds or significance tests except MT-Bench standard errors; one training run

availability.data: all training data released (github link above)

limits: Proof of concept: one large run, no seeds, mixture untested and not ablated; learning rate never cooled down and only 47000 steps.
Trained on 800B tokens, far below industrial models; lags later OLMo models on most lm-eval tasks.
No comparison against chain-of-thought-trained reasoning models; the only matched baseline is a 180B-token non-recurrent twin.
Fewer memorised facts: closed-book OBQA is weaker than reasoning-in-context OBQA.
Latent reasoning is less inspectable than verbalized CoT (oversight concern, Appendix A).
Several features (self-speculative decoding, continuous CoT) shown qualitatively or only with MT-Bench; self-speculative decoding has no number.
Post-training, RL and the interaction with MoE or linear attention are left as future work.
